props.eyebrow: Wedding and event music at a Colorado Springs resort
props.title: Garden of the Gods Resort and Club
props.lede: Garden of the Gods Resort looks out over the red rocks of Garden of the Gods and up to Pikes Peak. It was a private club for decades, and it’s one of the most beautiful places in Colorado for a wedding.

headingText.html: It has seven event spaces with five terraces and lawns between them, and most of them look right at the rocks.

props.title: Event spaces at Garden of the Gods Resort

spaces.name: Reflection Pool
spaces.facts: The Reflection Pool is the resort’s main outdoor ceremony site, for up to 220 guests seated.
spaces.why: A solo violin or a string quartet is a classic choice for a ceremony here.

spaces.name: Three Graces Ballroom and Terrace
spaces.facts: The Three Graces Ballroom is about 3,400 sq ft, for 220 to 300 guests. It has a glass-walled foyer and a private terrace with fire and water features.
spaces.why: Tejas works as a duo out on the private terrace or as a full band inside the Three Graces Ballroom.
spaces.alt: The Three Graces Ballroom set with navy-draped round tables and gold chairs.

spaces.name: The View at Kissing Camels
spaces.facts: The View at Kissing Camels is about 2,700 sq ft, for 130 to 150 guests, looking out over the golf course, Pikes Peak and the red rocks.
spaces.why: Meghan Clarisse’s country and Americana, solo or as a duo, for a dinner with that view.
spaces.alt: The View at Kissing Camels set with round dinner tables in front of tall windows facing the mountains.
spaces.credit: Photo: Garden of the Gods Resort

spaces.name: Garden Room and Terrace
spaces.facts: The Garden Room is a ballroom with windows, about 1,900 sq ft, for 100 to 150 guests, and it can be divided.
spaces.why: A jazz duo is a good size for the Garden Room.

spaces.name: Hill Room and Terrace
spaces.facts: The Hill Room is round, with picture windows facing the rocks and the mountains, for 40 to 60 guests.
spaces.why: René Moffatt’s own songs on acoustic guitar, for a small gathering.
spaces.alt: The round Hill Room set with long wooden tables and red napkins, with windows looking out toward the rocks.
spaces.credit: Photo: Garden of the Gods Resort

props.title: Planning music at Garden of the Gods Resort

rows.text: The resort offers full AV support for events, beyond what the band brings.
Every wedding has a planner or coordinator, and we plan load-in and setup with them and the resort’s sales and catering team.
The resort caters events in-house, and the reception includes a dance floor.
The Reflection Pool and the terraces are outdoors, and the resort offers backup space for an outdoor ceremony.
There’s complimentary valet and self-parking at the resort.

props.html: Questions about music at Garden of the Gods Resort

items.q: How much does live music add to a Garden of the Gods Resort wedding?
items.a: Mostly it’s the size of the act and how much of the day you’d like music for. A violinist at the Reflection Pool and a six-piece band in the Three Graces Ballroom sit at opposite ends. The pricing page has a general view of the Colorado market, and we’ll quote your date one-by-one.
